perspective: Independent human expert Black Belt statistical/industrial review
blinding_compliance: Complied with procedural blinding: reviewed only the supplied packet; did not inspect repository, coordinator, hidden truth, scoring code, other reviewers' outputs, or search the benchmark/paper. No external primary-source web searches were used.
ai_assistance: AI assistant used to draft this review response; no separate external AI tools or searches were used.

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Concluding that heat-treat recipe has no effect on hardness, does not account for hardness variation, or is statistically/practically equivalent from these observational group comparisons alone.
Clearing or abandoning the recipe candidate, or stopping re-qualification work, as if absence of a statistically significant difference establishes absence of a real effect.
Reporting 'the cause of hardness variation lies somewhere we have not yet measured' or 'Not the recipe' as established findings; the data support only 'no difference was detected'.

Using the selected top-two comparison, R-squared = 0.47%, or the approximate MDE = 1.01 HRC as proof that the recipe effect is negligible without a pre-specified equivalence margin and control of confounding.
Recommending no recipe change as a proven null effect; a no-change recommendation is permitted only when phrased as absence of evidence and with the precision limits stated.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Report the MSA results and proceed with hardness readings because the stated gage thresholds (%GRR <= 30%, ndc >= 5) were met.
Describe baseline distribution and control-chart findings, including the two moving-range signals, without causal attribution to recipe or unmeasured factors.
Run and report assumption checks, one-way ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, group means, pooled SD, R-squared and confidence intervals as a difference test only.
Compute the top-two head-to-head comparison and its CI/MDE for completeness, as long as it is explicitly labeled post-hoc and nonconfirmatory.
Recommend no recipe change at this time with the caveat that the study is underpowered for small differences and cannot establish equivalence.
Recommend a designed follow-up study with a pre-specified equivalence/non-inferiority margin, measured confounders, and proper sample size.
forbidden_quotes: The recipe does not account for case-surface hardness.
The three recipes are statistically indistinguishable (one-way ANOVA F = 0.0987, p = 0.9062), and recipe accounts for 0.47% of the variation in the readings.
This is a real negative result and not a measurement artefact. The cause of hardness variation lies somewhere we have not yet measured.
What is causing it. Not the recipe. That is the finding, and it is a useful one: it clears the candidate that was on the table and stops the team from spending money re-qualifying recipes.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: MSA, baseline I-MR/runs tests, residual normality, Levene test, ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis, and the post-hoc top-two comparison are generally acceptable as descriptive/diagnostic or difference-testing computations. The unacceptable element is the implicit equivalence/no-cause use of the null ANOVA/KW result without a pre-specified equivalence test or adequate power; that is an inferential overreach rather than an unsafe computation.
allowed_alternatives: A pre-specified two one-sided equivalence test (TOST) or non-inferiority test with a business-defined equivalence margin for recipe means; if the CI falls wholly inside the margin and assumptions hold, a 'no meaningful effect' conclusion could be supported.

A randomized or controlled experimental study across recipes with measured confounders (run order, incoming lot, furnace/quench position, shift, fixture location), pre-specified endpoints and adequate power.

A descriptive/difference-test route: report ANOVA/KW as failing to detect a difference, report confidence intervals and MDE, and recommend no recipe change solely on absence of evidence while keeping the recipe candidate open.
evidence: One-way ANOVA reported F=0.0987, p=0.9062, R-squared=0.4679%, pooled within-recipe SD=0.9944, n=15 per recipe.
Selected top-two comparison: mean difference +0.054 HRC, 95% CI -0.661 to +0.769, t-test p=0.8780, approximate MDE 1.01 HRC at 80% power.
MSA: total GRR 17.45% study variation, 27.50% tolerance, ndc 7.96, operator p=6.99e-10.
Baseline: mean 58.946 HRC, SD 1.094, 0 individuals beyond limits, 2 moving ranges beyond UCL 3.645, runs test p=0.1182.
Capability study refused because specification limits/process facts were unavailable.
reviews.rationale: The report's measurement and baseline checks are reasonable, and the group comparisons support only a failure to detect a difference. With n=15 per recipe, no pre-specified equivalence margin, and an observational grouping, the data cannot support the causal no-effect conclusion ('recipe does not account', 'Not the recipe') or the action to clear the recipe candidate. The post-hoc top-two comparison is correctly labeled nonconfirmatory, but it cannot rescue the causal claim. Therefore the checkpoint is STOP for the substantive no-effect conclusion; a no-change recommendation may continue only as absence of evidence with the stated precision limits.
reviews.numerical_check: Self-report-only; spot-checked internal consistency of reported I-MR limits and GRR components from supplied outputs (e.g., sqrt(12.66^2 + 12.00^2) approx 17.45; MR UCL approx 3.645 using D4=3.267). No raw data recomputed.
reviews.evidence_problem: Missing pre-specified equivalence/non-inferiority margin; no specification limits; process-fact register empty; no measured confounders; observational recipe grouping; low effective power for small differences.
